title.en: How to Become Attuned to City of Dalaran Dungeon as Horde in WoW: Forever
title.es: Cómo sintonizar con la mazmorra de la ciudad de Dalaran como una horda en WoW: Forever

summary.en: How to Become Attuned to City of Dalaran Dungeon as Horde in WoW: Forever...
summary.es: Cómo sintonizar con la mazmorra de la ciudad de Dalaran como horda en WoW: Forever...

contentHtml:
With level 30 now unlocked on the WoW: Forever Beta, players are looking forward to being able to run the City of Dalaran Dungeon. For Alliance, it seems pretty straightforward. Show up, speak to Image of Archmage Modera, receive the key and a quest, then walk right in. For Horde, however, it seems players will need to jump through some hoops to acquire the Key to Dalaran.

Farmerfarms has made an excellent video covering this attunement.



Initial Quests to Accept

QuestStartDescription
Prison Break InMagus Wordeen Voidglare, Tarren MillFind the traitors and recover their artifacts, then return to Magus Voidglare in Tarren Mill.
Key to the CityMagus Wordeen Voidglare, Tarren MillAcquire the Grimy Key for Magus Wordeen Voidglare.
Stone TokensKeeper Bel'varil, Tarren MillBring 10 Worn Stone Tokens to Keeper Bel'varil in Tarren Mill.

Hand in and accept next quests

QuestStartDescription
Dalaran PatrolsMagus Wordeen Voidglare, Tarren MillKill 6 Dalaran Summoners and 12 Elemental Slaves, then return to Magus Voidglare in Tarren Mill.
Bracers of BindingKeeper Bel'varil, Tarren MillBring 4 Bracers of Earth Binding to Keeper Bel'varil in Tarren Mill.

Hand in and accept next quest

QuestStartDescription
Blood in the StreetsMagus Wordeen Voidglare Tarren MillHand this quest in to Image of Archmage Modera outside Dalaran
Heart of DisruptionImage of Archmage Modera, Outside DalaranEnter the City of Dalaran and collect the Arcane Mote. Provides Dalaran Sewer Key, allowing entry into the city.


You will end this series of quests with Heart of Disruption in your quest log and the Dalaran Sewer Key in your keyring, ready for the City of Dalaran dungeon to become available.

summary.es: Ya están disponibles las tiradas de bonificación semanales...

contentHtml:
With the weekly reset, weekly bonus rolls are now available in Silvermoon!

Bonus Loot Rolls & Ascendant Venomstones


To unlock Weekly Rolls, players must complete In the Catalyst's Shadow and Prismatic Potential. These quests were available when Season 2 began, so you may have already completed them. If you haven't, head to Decimus in the Voidstorm to start the questline.

After turning in Prismatic Potential, players can earn one bonus roll per week at Orin in Silvermoon. The cost of the bonus roll is:
  • 5,000 Gold
  • 2,000 Voidlight Marl
  • 100 Veteran Crests
 


Good luck on your Bonus Rolls!

title.en: Devourer DH Moving in the Right Direction - Review of Patch 12.1.5 Changes
title.es: Devorador DH moviéndose en la dirección correcta - Revisión de los cambios del parche 12.1.5

summary.en: Devourer DH Moving in the Right Direction - Review of Patch 12.1.5 Changes...
summary.es: Devorador DH moviéndose en la dirección correcta - Revisión de los cambios del parche 12.1.5...

contentHtml:
Our Devourer DH writer, Voodoosaurus, breaks down all the Devourer DH changes in Patch 12.1.5 and how it'll impact gameplay when the next patch launches on October 13th.

Devourer DH Overview

Devourer 12.1.5 Changes

Devourer Demon Hunter is the newest specialization in World of Warcraft, joining the roster with 12.0 and the launch of Midnight. Despite being so new, Devourer has already received multiple rounds of large changes, and this trend continues in 12.1.5, featuring even more sweeping changes to Devourer. In this article, I aim to dive into what the problems facing Devourer are, the changes coming in, and the impact of these changes.

How did we get here?

Coming into 12.1, targeted changes were made to reduce the power of Void Metamorphosis, reducing the scaling of Collapsing Star through a targeted nerf to Impending Apocalypse, and a reduction to the inside Void Meta component of our Mastery, Mastery: Monster Within. Coupled with the loss of our S1 tier set, Demon Hunter Devourer 12.0 Class Set 4pc, this amounted to a large loss of damage from inside Void Metamorphosis, and a large hit to  Annihilator. These changes, plus our Reap empowering tier set in season 2 ( Demon Hunter Devourer 12.1 Class Set 4pc), pushed us into playing  Void-Scarred, although last-minute buffs to Collapsing Star and small nerfs to Reap and Eradicate maintained  Annihilator's viability in keys, especially in higher, more coordinated groups.

This shift to  Void-Scarred led to us focusing more on the melee-oriented playstyle, focusing our damage around abilities such as Hungering Slash, The Hunt, Voidsurge, and Reap. This playstyle saw us aim to jump into and out of melee often, rapidly cycling our Void Metamorphosis to leverage more resets of abilities. This offered an entirely new playstyle, although one which was divisive in the player base. It also highlighted many issues with Devourer, separate from those that  Annihilator already had. So what are those?
  • AFKing: Due to the power of Rolling Torment and the strength gained from entering Void Metamorphosis, it's correct for  Void-Scarred to AFK when fighting 2 or more targets once you've gotten to your second Eradicate. This allows you to cycle quicker, trading fairly weak damage at the end of your Void Metamorphosis for more entrances of Void Metamorphosis. This behavior is something that most players, and Blizzard themselves, do not like.
  • Ignoring Collapsing Star: Collapsing Star is billed as the core button for Devourer, building up to it in your Void Metamorphosis, and having it be a satisfying and powerful component of your rotation. Our entire apex talents ( Midnight, Midnight, and Midnight) are even built around empowering it! However, Collapsing Star was weakened significantly going into 12.1, and has anti-synergy with  Void-Scarred. Rolling Torment converts souls you consume in Void Metamorphosis into its powerful buff, but Collapsing Star uses those collected souls, reducing the overall buff gained from Rolling Torment. This loss in buff does not make up for how weak Collapsing Star is, especially since  Void-Scarred plays with Soul Glutton, meaning they get one Collapsing Star at most. Collapsing Star being so weak also means that  Void-Scarred builds do not take our Apex talents.
  • 180 Playstyle Difference: Devourer's two hero talent options,  Void-Scarred and  Annihilator, feature incredibly different playstyles, to the point where they are essentially different specs. This leads to almost whiplash in playstyle, where players who are playing Devourer, and who seek to play the best options, can be playing different specs from patch to patch, or even boss to boss, even though they are still a Devourer. While many enjoy the current playstyle, Blizzard has communicated to us that the large changes between the two trees are not something they like.
  • Bottom Gate Points: Devourer's bottom gate is incredibly rich with points that are needed for the spec to function: Eradicate is needed whenever fighting 2 or more targets, the entire left side leading to The Hunt is needed for  Void-Scarred to function, Calamitous is needed for all builds, Devourer's Bite is needed for any builds using the melee talents, and the Apex, Midnight, is needed for all Collapsing Star builds. This puts a large amount of pressure on our talent choices and cost, needing to give up large parts of playstyle or identity to make builds function.
  • Collapsing Star QOL: While Collapsing Star is our large flashy button, it also comes with annoyances. It's designed with a long cast time to amplify the weight of this cast. To offset the downside of casting this during our cooldowns, where our resources are constantly drained, the cast of Collapsing Star incurs a short window where the constant drain is slowed considerably. To get in front of the edge cases where someone would look to constantly cast and cancel Collapsing Star to take advantage of this slow, Blizzard implemented a 5s lockout on Collapsing Star as soon as you have started the cast. This means that if your cast were to fail due to your target dying, if your target were to move out of your 25 yard range, if you had to cancel it due to a mechanic occurring, or even if you collected enough souls to cast 2 back to back, you would not be able to. It would incur a hard 5s cooldown no matter what, and constantly lead to over-capping of souls. This behavior is incredibly frustrating for many players, and has been a constant source of friction.
Knowing what issues players have been facing, what changes are coming down the pipeline?

What's Changing?

The changes for Devourer came mostly in two sections, with the first bringing us the largest portion:
DEMON HUNTER
Devourer
  • Developers’ notes: Cancelled casts of Collapsing Star have been a noted pain point since Devourer’s introduction, and the changes in this update are aimed at alleviating some of that frustration.
    Until now, there has been a cooldown enforced on Collapsing Star after it was interrupted or cancelled; this was in place to discourage gameplay that would capitalize on the slowed Fury drain during its cast to extend Void Metamorphosis and land a Collapsing Star at the ‘right’ time. While it was effective at that primary goal, the cooldown was also jarring for players when a cast was interrupted or manually cancelled for very normal gameplay reasons. We hope the changes to Collapsing Star in this update will be able to find a middle ground where normal gameplay will not be punished and rarely notice the new underlying restriction, while still minimizing the opportunity and incentive to manipulate its slowed Fury drain mechanic.
    Second, because of Collapsing Star’s long cast time combined with its medium range, the circumstances where Collapsing Star would be cancelled by its target moving out of range were too common. We’re giving Collapsing Star more wiggle room to finish its cast by giving it extra range after its cast begins.
  • Collapsing Star now has increased range after it starts casting, reducing the circumstances where it will fail from the target moving out of range.
  • Collapsing Star no longer goes on cooldown for 5 seconds when its cast is cancelled.
  • Collapsing Star will now only slow Fury drain during its cast for a limited time.
    • if Collapsing Star’s cast is cancelled then cast again, it will only be able to slow Fury drain for a total time of approximately 1.5 full casts.
    • After that time limit has been reached, Fury drain will resume in full regardless of whether or not a cast is interrupted or starts again.
Void-Scarred
  • Developers’ notes: The Void-Scarred talent tree had multiple powerful bonuses that all centered around entering Void Metamorphosis, which was discouraging players from casting Collapsing Star because doing so would delay how long it would be until entering Void Metamorphosis and benefiting from those bonuses again. Collapsing Star is intended to be a feature ability of Devourer’s rotation regardless of which Hero Talents are selected, so some of Void-Scarred’s bonuses will now be granted by casting Collapsing Star instead of only being granted by entering Void Metamorphosis.
  • Demonic Intensity now causes Collapsing Star to reset the cooldown of The Hunt.
  • Demonic Intensity’s empower effect for The Hunt now increases its damage by 30%.
  • Violent Transformation now resets the cooldown of Soul Immolation.
  • Violent Transformation no longer resets the cooldown of The Hunt.
  • Violent Transformation no longer increases the damage of The Hunt (was 25%) or causes it to reset the cooldown of Soul Immolation.
  • Monster Rising now increases Intellect by 10% while not in demon form (was 15%).
  • Monster Rising now increases Collapsing Star damage by 20% (was 15%).
These changes were broadly targeted at  Void-Scarred and Collapsing Star, and aimed to address a few of the concerns raised in the first section. The Collapsing Star changes are huge QOL improvements and make the ability function and feel incredibly good. It's much less punishing with the range increase and the removal of its cooldown, allowing you to quickly cancel a cast if something were to interrupt you. The changes to fury drain ensure that no small edge cases can occur where it's correct to repeatedly cast and then cancel Collapsing Star, while still maintaining the fury drain should you need to cancel to reposition.

The  Void-Scarred changes are much more wide reaching, aiming to break the quick melee cycle playstyle and reintroduce casting Collapsing Star. On live, The Hunt is currently reset upon entering Void Metamorphosis, allowing you to use your empowers at the start of your window. This is being changed to be reset by casting Collapsing Star, all but ensuring the ability will be used in our rotation. This does mean that long Void Metamorphosis windows, using Emptiness would get significantly more casts of The Hunt, and as such it was nerfed to compensate ( Demonic Intensity went from 25% to 30%, but the 25% from Violent Transformation was removed fully). Additionally, they aimed to reduce the frequency of Soul Immolation resets that would happen from casting The Hunt this often, moving its reset to entering Void Metamorphosis. The idea behind these changes is to unify the playstyles of  Annihilator and  Void-Scarred, giving  Void-Scarred a reason to press Collapsing Star, and no reason to AFK due to this increased power behind it. These changes did accomplish this, as  Void-Scarred loves to cast Collapsing Star, but further increased the friction in the bottom gate, leaving it impossible for  Void-Scarred to take all the points needed to fill out its various packages. Thankfully, Blizzard came through with additional notes the week after.
DEMON HUNTER
Devourer
  • Soulforged Blades now increases the critical strike chance of Hungering Slash and Voidblade by 18% (was 15%).
  • Voidpurge now reduces the cooldown of Void Ray during Void Metamorphosis by 2.5 seconds (was 2 seconds).
  • Developers’ notes: In addition to the Void-Scarred changes, we are shuffling some talents around to make it a little easier for builds to access core functional effects. The final gate was very dense and two of its talents are moving to the middle gate. The final gate’s capstone talents also notably included effects that are core building blocks: The Hunt is featured for Void-Scarred builds, and Eradicate is a key component of any build’s AoE damage. Those two talents are moving to more accessible locations in the middle gate of the tree, with other talents moving into their capstone positions.
  • Many talents have changed positions.
  • Demonic Instinct now connects to the talent one row down and one column to the left.
  • Devourer’s Edge now connects to the talent one row down and one column to the right.
The changes to the talent tree are actually quite extensive, and seek to alleviate pressure in the base of the tree. Rather than going over every change, see the talent tree below, where moved nodes and new connections are highlighted in green



By moving nodes like Eradicate and The Hunt higher in the tree, these options are now MUCH more accessible for all builds, and even open up additional options, such as  Annihilator taking The Hunt. The additional connections now also provide more pathing options, especially since one of Demonic Instinct or Devourer's Edge would be taken due to pathing to Emptiness. These changes also make it much easier to take our Apex, and the movement of Star Fragments adds additional power to Collapsing Star.

The Impacts



These changes together seek to address almost all of the issues which were raised at the start of this article. Eradicate and The Hunt are much easier to take, Collapsing Star has had large QOL changes applied to it,  Void-Scarred now seeks to use Collapsing Star, no longer wants to AFK, and has a playstyle much more unified with  Annihilator, meaning there won't be large differences patch to patch. The rotation is also just FUN, as it combines all the best parts of Devourer, incorporating the melee combo, Reap, long Void Metamorphosis with Emptiness, and Collapsing Star! You'll see yourself rushing into and out of melee, dealing damage before running back out and dropping large Collapsing Stars on your enemies. It maintains some of the feel that current  Void-Scarred has, while still feeling like it shares a spec with  Annihilator, rather than being its own thing. Unfortunately, it is not all sunshine and roses.

The introduction of Collapsing Star and the multiple resets to The Hunt lead to situations where you are immobile or in forced movement incredibly often. You can often get 4-5 casts of Collapsing Star in your Void Metamorphosis windows, meaning that you will cast The Hunt directly before it 4-5 times per cooldown. This leads to windows where you have no control over your character (due to the long cast + rush of The Hunt, and the long cast of Collapsing Star) for roughly 5s at a time, most of which is spent in melee.  Void-Scarred currently suffers from its difficulty to play on live servers, with the melee combo being dangerous for players. This new iteration seeks to have you do this more often, with The Hunt's rush being much longer than Voidblade. Additionally, the fury pause from Voidrush only triggers on The Hunt's cast completion and is quite short, leading to situations where Void Metamorphosis can and will drop during your cast.

The talent tree changes also leave the talents in the base of the tree pretty subpar. Aside from Devourer's Bite, Calamitous and Emptiness, many of the talents down here are fairly weak. Soulforged Blades, Voidglare Boon, Voidrush, and Rolling Torment are very subpar and are only taken for pathing in some situations. Singular Strikes is still bugged to give the 50% bonus to a random target. The Apex is still fairly weak, due in part to reducing Collapsing Star's ability to crit. While there are strong talents, moving Eradicate and The Hunt out of this gate leaves many of these options not desirable, and future iteration will likely be needed to improve the options down here, or to introduce and offer new ones.

With the release date of 12.1.5 now announced, we won't be seeing changes to Devourer for this patch cycle, but the steps they've taken are steps in the right direction, and further iteration on the spec in the future sets up an exciting future where Devourer can successfully incorporate all aspects of its kit, without having to sacrifice parts of its kit or fun.

summary.en: Massive Heroic and Mythic Ula'tek Nerfs with Weekly Reset...
summary.es: Nerfs Ula 'tek Heroicoos y míticos masivos con restablecimiento semanal...

contentHtml:
Blizzard has announced massive nerfs to Ula'tek on Heroic and Mythic with the weekly reset.
Blizzard
View Original
Hello raiders!

The following Ula’tek raid encounter adjustments will arrive with scheduled weekly maintenance (October 6 in this region).

Dungeons and Raids

  • The Venomous Abyss
    • Ula’tek
      • General
        • Spectral Coils damage reduced by 20% on Heroic and Mythic difficulties.
      • Stage 02
        • Warden’s Protection damage reduced by 80%.
        • Reduced the number of ground targets during Virulent Spit.
        • Grasping Fangs periodic damage reduced by 30% on Heroic and Mythic difficulties.
        • Blight Vein duration reduced to 4 seconds on Heroic and Mythic difficulties (was 6 seconds).
      • Stage 03
        • Blightscale Shrieker health reduced by 20% on Heroic and Mythic difficulties.
        • Blightscale Clutch health reduced by 20% on Heroic and Mythic difficulties.
        • Slithering Clutch health reduced by 20% on Mythic difficulties.
        • Circling Prey raid damage reduced by 30% on Heroic and Mythic difficulties.
        • Adjusted the Drain Rate of Serpent’s Bite so you no longer need more than 3 people to soak regardless of raid size.
        • Toxic Burn damage reduced by 30% on Mythic difficulty.
        • The number of waves that emit from a tail during Caustic Waves reduced to 3 on Mythic difficulty (was 7).

title.es: Johnny Cash anuncia que Stitches vuelve a ser hostil en WoW: Forever

summary.en: Johnny Cash Announces that Stitches is Hostile Again in WoW: Forever...
summary.es: Johnny Cash anuncia que Stitches vuelve a ser hostil en WoW: Forever...

contentHtml:
Johnny Cash has announced on X (Twitter) that Stitches is hostile in WoW: Forever once again.

Stitches is one of the most famous NPCs in WoW: Classic. Found in Duskwood, he patrols the road, striking down anyone who gets too close. During last week's Beta build, players noticed that Stitches was marked as a neutral mob, and this has now been fixed, according to Johnny Cash on X (Twitter).

Tweet #2107204533944504382


If you're entering Duskwood, make sure to watch out for an angry Stitches!
